problem:
Suppose $T:V\to W$ is a linear map and $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}$ and $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2},{c}_{3}}$ are the bases of the vector spaces $V$ and $W$, respectively. Find the matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the map $T$ relative to these bases, if 

$\,$ $T({b}_{1})=-2{c}_{1}+4{c}_{2}-2{c}_{3}\,$ and $\,T({b}_{2})=3{c}_{2}-7{c}_{3}+{c}_{1}.$

activity_context.topic_title: The Matrix of a Linear Map Relative to Two Bases

feedback.problem:
Suppose $T:V\to W$ is a linear map and $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}}$ and $C={{c}_{1},{c}_{2}}$ are the bases of the vector spaces $V$ and $W$, respectively. Find the matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the map $T$ relative to these bases, if 

$$
[T({b}_{1})]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 7\end{aligned}],\,[T({b}_{2})]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -5\end{aligned}],\,[T({b}_{3})]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
Recall that $[T]_{B|C}$ is the matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1}),$ $T({b}_{2}),$ and $T({b}_{3})$ relative to the basis $C.$ Therefore,

$$
[T]_{B|C}=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & 1 \\ 7 & -5 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$
